summary: Anthropic launched Claude Tag, a Slack integration allowing teams to add Claude as a channel member that can be tagged to receive delegated tasks, retain cross-channel memory, work asynchronously over hours or days, and act proactively, built on Opus 4.8 and replacing the existing Claude-in-Slack app for Enterprise and Team customers.

mechanisms.reason: Anthropic describes internal delegation of work to many parallel Claude instances rather than human seats performing the tasks directly.
mechanisms.quote: we now spend much more of our time delegating tasks to many Claudes in parallel.

mechanisms.reason: Autonomous, long-running scheduled tasks and asynchronous multi-day work imply higher aggregate token/inference consumption per delegated task.
mechanisms.quote: It can also schedule tasks for itself, pursuing a project autonomously over hours or days.

mechanisms.reason: Persistent cross-channel context building implies growing memory/context state carried per deployment, distinct from raw token volume.
mechanisms.quote: Claude builds context by remembering relevant information from the channels it’s in, and can plan out tasks to complete in the future.

practices.reason: Describes a concrete task-decomposition, tool-use, and asynchronous multi-agent delegation pattern already used internally at scale, which teams could replicate for their own agent workflows.
practices.quote: Tag @Claude with a request in simple terms and it’ll break its task down into stages and then work through them in turn, using the tools it has access to.

practices.reason: Existing Claude-in-Slack deployments must be migrated to the new product within a stated window, creating scheduled integration work for admins.
practices.quote: Claude Tag replaces the existing Claude in Slack app. To migrate, administrators can opt in within 30 days.

notable_reason: Anthropic discloses that 65% of its own product team's code is now produced via internal delegation to Claude, a concrete internal data point on agentic workflow adoption at scale.
